subject: Meteorology
title: Lightning Safety
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lightning Safety.

hook.text: Lightning kills about 2,000 people worldwide each year—most struck outdoors during recreational activities.

buildup.text: The 30-30 rule: if the flash-to-thunder delay is under 30 seconds, seek shelter; wait 30 minutes after the last flash.

discovery.text: A hard-topped vehicle or enclosed building offers strong protection—rubber soles and tires won't save you.

twist.text: Lightning can strike the same place repeatedly—the Empire State Building is hit about 25 times per year.

climax.text: Most lightning deaths occur not from direct hits but from ground current—electricity spreading through wet soil.

punchline.text: When thunder roars, go indoors—it really is that simple.

quiz.question: How do most lightning fatalities occur?
options: Ground current spreading through wet soil
